attacks.claim: The announcement promises text alerts for every cardholder, but the SMS option is hidden on juvenile cards. The public statement is inaccurate for a whole class of cardholders and sets wrong expectations for families.
attacks.evidence: Announcement text says exactly: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." vs. "juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: SMS-only patrons may have no working notice channel. The SMS option can replace email, and the artifact does not confirm email is still sent. The 'previous method' fallback for the cap event and the sms_holds rollback is therefore undefined, so holds could go unannounced, contrary to 'no alert is lost'.
attacks.evidence: "in addition to (or instead of) the current email" / "every opted-in patron gets hold notices by their previous method (email or automated phone call, kept on file)" / ABSENT: confirmation that email or phone is still sent to SMS-only patrons

attacks.claim: The spend-cap fallback moves notices to automated phone calls, which the $900/month SMS cap does not limit and the $460/month SMS forecast (BM-26-14) does not cover. Call cost is unforecast and uncapped.
attacks.evidence: "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)" / ABSENT: any call-channel cost forecast, cap, or alert

attacks.claim: Locker accessibility claims (high contrast, audio guidance, adjustable text) are unverified. The QA table covers screen readers only for the opt-in web form, and no locker row tests the touchscreen, audio, or contrast for the feature with the most physical-access risk.
attacks.evidence: "high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack, and adjustable text size" / QA row "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS" / ABSENT: locker accessibility test results

attacks.claim: Batched texts may give one code for several locker holds, or holds at several locations. A single code cannot open multiple cells, and the artifact does not say whether each hold gets its own code.
attacks.evidence: "extra holds are batched into one message" and "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913" vs. "Codes are single-use"

attacks.claim: Locker lockout after 5 wrong codes locks the cell and alerts staff, but the lockers run 24/7 and staff are not on site overnight. No after-hours recovery path is defined, and the hold may be stranded in a locked cell until the deadline passes.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff" and "vendor SLA 4h on-site" (applies to "any locker bank offline"); ABSENT: after-hours recovery path for a locked cell or hold reassignment.

attacks.claim: The locker_pickup rollback requires staff to physically move items across three banks, with no bound on volume or time. Remap was tested on 1,200 rows, not on live volume. Codes already sent to patrons are not stated to be invalidated, so patrons could arrive at a locker with a still-valid code, and the notice channel for non-SMS patrons is not specified.
attacks.evidence: "staff move items to the holds shelf, hold deadlines extend 3 days and patrons are notified of the new location" / "tested in staging on 1,200 rows" / ABSENT: code invalidation and notice channel for non-SMS patrons

attacks.claim: Lockers go live for all holds at three branches at once, with no ramp beyond the 64-card staff pilot. A physical fault at this scale would be large before rollback takes effect, and the physical rollback is expensive.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders" / "Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)."

attacks.claim: Consent records (timestamp, IP, checkbox version) and the phone number are kept in the patron record with no stated retention limit. The 30-day purge covers only the notification log. Retention after STOP is unstated, which conflicts with the library's minimization policy and leaves TCPA-style consent evidence undefined after opt-out.
attacks.evidence: "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record" / "STOP ... clears the opt-in flag"

attacks.claim: Production delivery was not proven. QA ran against the production provider account in test mode, and the spend-cap test used a $5 cap rather than $900. Carrier filtering, 10DLC throughput, and the fallback under real load at 210k-cardholder scale are unverified before the all-cardholder launch.
attacks.evidence: "against the production SMS provider account in test mode" and "Spend cap reached (test cap $5)"

attacks.claim: The juvenile and guardian path is not fully addressed. Hold notices for a minor's card, including locker location and pickup code, go to the guardian's phone, and the artifact does not state whether this follows juvenile-record handling rules or minor-consent requirements.
attacks.evidence: "guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account"

attacks.claim: STOP depends on the provider and signed webhook, with no lag alert or reconciliation for the flag. The provider's own STOP handling mitigates this, but the library-side flag can drift.
attacks.evidence: "STOP ... is honored by the provider and our signed webhook, which clears the opt-in flag" / Monitoring alerts only on "webhook signature failures > 0"

attacks.claim: Quiet-hours and batched messages release together at 08:00, a burst that could strain provider throughput. Queue depth is shown on the dashboard but has no alert.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00" / "queue depth" appears on the dashboard only

attacks.claim: A locker bank offline for more than 10 minutes pages staff, but there is no fallback for codes already sent for that bank. The 4-hour vendor SLA leaves patrons unable to collect for hours.
attacks.evidence: "any locker bank offline > 10 min (pages branch manager + vendor; vendor SLA 4 h on-site)"

attacks.claim: Locker touchscreen and audio language are unspecified. Spanish is supported for texts only, so Spanish-preferring patrons may be stuck at the locker.
attacks.evidence: "English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference" applies to texts; ABSENT: locker UI language.

attacks.claim: Audio guidance is available only through a headphone jack, so a blind patron without headphones gets no spoken instructions at the locker.
There is no documented exit path for opted-in phone numbers and consent records if the SMS provider is changed. Migration would require re-consent or an undescribed export.
attacks.evidence: "numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days and patrons are emailed"

attacks.claim: Deleting consent records 30 days after permanent SMS withdrawal removes the evidence needed to defend against consent disputes. Legal should confirm retention before this becomes the default.
attacks.evidence: "If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days"

attacks.claim: The remap script's rerun safety and idempotence are not evidenced, and holds in transit during the remap are not addressed.
